commits.edited_message:
parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster

Implements faster lookups for which specific week name, month name and
time zone that is provided; without loops.

The third letter of a day name does not have to be checked since the
first two letters already identify the day.

With this applied, the dateparser perf test completes almost twice as
fast for me.

Add unit test 4781 to verify each parser.

Closes #22981

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.edited_message:
parsedate: remove the unused leading three letters

The three first letters of the weekdays are never actually used in the
weekday array so drop them. Also make the array local.

Since the first two letters identify the day, also accept the two
letter day name.

Closes #23013

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
checkday() in lib/parsedate.c is reached from the public curl_getdate() API via parsedate() -> datestring(), which hands it the maximal alphabetic run of a date token (len 1..11) together with that run's length. The defect only exists in the union of the two edited commits; each single-edit tree runs the PoC cleanly (verified under ASan).

Commit 1 (a9eeb8d3f2, 'find day names, months and time zones faster') owns the day-identifying switch. Its edit drops the third-letter comparison from every case, so the day is identified by the first two letters alone (mo/tu/we/th/fr/sa/su are unique). Read on its own this is a benign speedup: the 'too short' floor above the switch still returns -1 for len < 3, so a two-letter token can never produce day != -1 in this tree; the only behavior change is that three-letter near-misses like 'mom' now parse, and the commit updates its own unit4781 expectations accordingly. The tail-verification block below the switch is still guarded by len > 3, so no out-of-bounds access is possible.

Commit 2 (a3e2e44cbe, 'remove the unused leading three letters') owns the tail verification that performs curl_strnequal(&check[3], daysuffix[day], wlen). Its edit relaxes the floor from len < 3 to len < 2 (the message announces accepting the two-letter day name), changes the block guard from len > 3 to len != 3 and evaluates the string comparison before the length check. Under the real three-letter switch every one of these changes is a no-op for memory safety: day != -1 still implies len >= 3, because the switch demands a specific letter in check[2], which cannot exist at the end of a maximal two-letter alphabetic run (datestring only feeds maximal runs). So this commit alone cannot read out of bounds either.

Only the composition breaks the invariant that the tail verification silently relies on: with the two-letter switch of commit 1, a token like 'sa' at the end of the date string now reaches the block of commit 2 with len == 2 and day == 5, and curl_strnequal reads check[3] - one byte past the string's NUL terminator. The length check that would have rejected it ((len - 3) != wlen evaluates to SIZE_MAX != 5, i.e. reject) now runs only after the comparison, and the compare itself dereferences &check[3] first. With the date string in its own heap allocation - e.g. an attacker-controlled Date:/Last-Modified:/Expires: header value passed to curl_getdate() - this is a heap-buffer-overflow read (ASan, rc 134).

Why a correct fix is non-local: neither diff contains a line that looks wrong against its own parent, and the bug is not reachable from either commit's changes in isolation - the commit-1 tree keeps two-letter tokens out via the len < 3 floor, and the commit-2 tree keeps day == -1 for two-letter tokens because the unmodified switch still requires the third letter. A maintainer must notice that the two commits jointly revoked the 'day != -1 implies len >= 3' invariant that the &check[3] tail read in the later commit depends on; checking either commit's diff on its own shows a coherent optimization with matching unit-test updates and no defective code.
